record.title: Sum rules for the three singlets in the cyclic model
record.statement:
For odd $N=2n+1$, consider the cyclic spin-chain Hamiltonian with parameters $\lambda,\zeta$ and its three translation-invariant zero-energy singlets $\Psi_N^a$, indexed by $a=0,\pm$, with components $\psi_\mu^a$ in spin configurations $\mu$. Let $\nu_1(\mu)$ be the number of spins equal to $1$ in $\mu$. **The cyclic singlet sum-rule conjecture.** With the stated normalisation, the square norm of each singlet factorises into two polynomials in $\zeta,\lambda$ with positive integer coefficients. Along $\lambda=\zeta$,

$$
\lVert\Psi_N^a(\zeta)\rVert^2=3^{-2n}\left(\sum_\mu\zeta^{\nu_1(\mu)}\psi_\mu^a\right)\left(\sum_\mu\zeta^{-\nu_1(\mu)}\psi_\mu^a\right),\qquad a=0,\pm.
$$

For $\Psi_N^0$, along the same line,

$$
\sum_\mu\zeta^{\nu_1(\mu)}\psi_\mu^0=3^{2n}\zeta^{2n+1}\psi_{11\dots1}^0.
$$

The source presents these as open questions supported by exact diagonalisation through $N=7$.
record.source_name: Christian Hagendorf, “Spin chains with dynamical lattice supersymmetry”, arXiv:1207.0357 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0357

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2012). “The present work leads to many open questions.”

record.title: Congruence pattern for the function S(a) modulo 3
record.statement:
Let $S(a)$ be the rational-valued function defined, for each nonnegative integer $a$, by the right-hand side of equation (7.11):

$$
S(a)=\sum_{0\le j\le\frac{a-1}2}\;\sum_{0\le i\le 2j+2\{\frac{a-1}2\}}(-2)^j\binom ai\binom{a+2j+2\{\frac{a-1}2\}-i}{2j+2\{\frac{a-1}2\}-i}
\left[\binom{\lfloor\frac a2\rfloor+j}{2j+2\{\frac{a-1}2\}}+\binom{\lfloor\frac a2\rfloor+\frac 12+j}{2j+2\{\frac{a-1}2\}}\right].
$$

**Congruence-pattern conjecture.** One has

$$
S(a)\equiv \begin{cases} 0\pmod 3&\text{if }a=0\text{ or }3^{2k+1}\le a\le 3^{2k+2}-1\text{ for some integer }k\ge 0,\\ -1\pmod 3&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases}
$$

This pattern strengthens the preceding congruence for $q\equiv 1\pmod 8$, which gives $S(a)\equiv0\pmod p$ on a specified interval. It is motivated by computer experiments, and no proof or resolution is supplied in the source.

record.title: Conjecture on the structure of the sets of bounded-coefficient $(q;q)_m$ polynomials
record.statement:
Let $h$ be a positive integer, and let $S_h$ be the set of all nonnegative integers $m$ such that every coefficient of $(q;q)_m$ lies between $-h$ and $h$, with at least one coefficient having absolute value $h$. For $h>16$, let $i(h)$ denote a positive integer when $S_h$ is nonempty. **The bounded-coefficient set conjecture.** Either $S_h$ is empty or $S_h=\{i(h)\}$ for $h>16$, and

$$
i(h_1)>i(h_2)\quad\text{when }h_1>h_2>16.
$$

Moreover, for $h>5$, there is a positive integer $M(h)$ such that

$$
S_1\cup S_2\cup\dots\cup S_h=\{0,1,2,\dots,M(h)\}.
$$

The conjecture summarizes the observed structure of the sets $S_h$ in the computed data: beyond $h=16$, each set is predicted to contain at most one value, with these values decreasing as $h$ increases, while the cumulative sets are predicted to form an initial interval of nonnegative integers for $h>5$.
record.source_name: Alexander Berkovich and Ali K. Uncu, “On some polynomials and series of Bloch-Polya Type”, arXiv:1705.07504 (2017).
record.references:

record.title: The length-restricted antipalindrome sum conjecture
record.statement:
An **antipalindrome** is a natural number whose canonical base-$2$ expansion is an antipalindromic word, meaning that the word equals the complement of its reversal. An even integer has an even least significant bit. For an odd integer length $n\geq 9$, consider even integers whose canonical base-$2$ expansions have length $n$.

**The length-restricted antipalindrome sum conjecture.** Every even integer of length $n$, for $n$ odd and $n\geq 9$, is the sum of at most $10$ antipalindromes of length $n-3$.

The conjecture is intended to be proved using nondeterministic pushdown automata, but the authors' computations were incomplete because their program ran out of space. They hoped to establish it as a theorem in a future version; its truth would imply that every even natural number is the sum of at most $13$ antipalindromes.
record.source_name: Aayush Rajasekaran, Jeffrey Shallit and Tim Smith, “Sums of Palindromes: an Approach via Automata”, arXiv:1706.10206 (2017).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.10206

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

record.title: Generalized oriented Hamilton cycle discrepancy conjecture via s-star
record.statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph on $n\ge 3$ vertices. For distinct vertices $u,v$, call them **non-adjacent** if neither directed arc joins them, and define

$$
s^*(D)=\min\{d(u)+d(v)-n:u\ne v\in V(D),\ \{uv,vu\}\cap A(D)=\emptyset\}
$$

when $D$ has a pair of non-adjacent vertices; set $s^*(D)=n-2$ when $D$ is a tournament. For an oriented Hamilton cycle $C$, let $\sigma_{\max}(C)$ be the larger of its numbers of forward and backward arcs. **s-star discrepancy conjecture.** If $s^*(D)\ge 0$, then there is a Hamilton oriented cycle $C$ in $D$ such that

$$
\sigma_{\max}(C)\ge \left\lceil\frac{n+s^*(D)}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

This is stated as another natural generalization of the cited Dirac-type theorem. The source presents it as open and reports supporting results for the related conjectures.
record.source_name: Jiangdong Ai, Qiwen Guo, Gregory Gutin, Yongxin Lan, Qi Shao, Anders Yeo and Yacong Zhou, “Oriented discrepancy of Hamilton cycles in oriented graphs satisfying Ore-type condition”, arXiv:2501.05968 (2026).
record.references:

record.title: The Pell-equation existence conjecture for $(1,1)$-antimagic graph unions
record.statement:
Let $P_3$ be the path on three vertices. For a graph $H$, a **$(1,1)$-antimagic labeling** is an antimagic labeling whose vertex sums are exactly $1,2,\ldots,|V(H)|$. **Pell-equation existence conjecture.** Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
(2n+1)^2-2(2m+1)^2=-1.
$$

Then there exist a graph $G$ and an integer $c$ such that

$$
|V(G+cP_3)|=n,\qquad |E(G+cP_3)|=m,
$$

and $G+cP_3$ has a $(1,1)$-antimagic labeling. The preceding discussion motivates this as an existence question for graphs with prescribed numbers of vertices and edges satisfying the Pell equation, especially because components isomorphic to $P_3$ are forced in the relevant setting; the supplied text does not state that the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Wei-Tian Li and Po-Wen Yang, “Constructing the antimagic labelings for double stars union paths on three vertices”, arXiv:2503.15296 (2025).

record.title: Linear-time computation of the tetra-separation decomposition
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a 4-connected finite graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The **linear-time decomposition algorithm conjecture.** There is an algorithm that returns the tetra-separation decomposition of $G$ from the main decomposition theorem in time

$$
\mathcal{O}(n+m).
$$

The claim is motivated by the existence of algorithms constructing 5-lean tree-decompositions of finite graphs in parameterized near-linear time. It remains an algorithmic conjecture because the source states that the proposed linear-time conversion to the tetra-separation decomposition is believed to exist, rather than proving it.

record.title: Starlike rayless-tree characterization conjecture for compact generated ultrametric spaces
record.statement:
Let $(X,d)$ be an infinite ultrametric space. A labeled ray is a ray equipped with a labeling that generates the indicated ultrametric space. A tree is **starlike** if it has exactly one vertex of degree greater than $2$, and **rayless** if it contains no ray. **Starlike rayless-tree characterization conjecture.** The following statements are equivalent:

1. $(X,d)$ is the completion of a totally bounded proper subset $X_0\subsetneq X$ generated by a labeled ray.
2. There exists a starlike rayless tree $T$ with a labeling $l:V(T)\to\mathbb R^+$ such that $(X,d)$ is a compact ultrametric space generated by $T(l)$.

The claim is presented as a partial generalization of an earlier theorem in the source. No resolution status is supplied.

record.title: Existence conjecture for plane curves with prescribed graded Betti partition
record.statement: Let $C:f=0$ be a reduced plane curve that is not free, with $t(C)=\sum_{j=1}^{m-2}\epsilon_j\geq 1$, and let $\pi_C$ be the ordered partition of $t(C)$ whose parts are the positive integers $\epsilon_j$. A curve has class $tT_{\pi}$ when $t(C)=t$ and $\pi_C=\pi$. **Existence conjecture.** For each $t\geq 1$ and each ordered partition $\pi$ of $t$, the set of plane curves of class $tT_{\pi}$ is not empty. This conjecture predicts that every ordered partition arising from the graded Betti numbers of a non-free reduced plane curve is realized by at least one plane curve; the supplied text gives no resolution or partial evidence.

record.title: Győri et al.'s linear Turán conjecture for linear paths in 3-graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex **linear 3-graph**, meaning that any two distinct hyperedges of $G$ intersect in at most one vertex. A **linear path** of length $k$ is the unique acyclic Berge path of length $k$, and therefore has $2k+1$ vertices.

**Győri et al.'s linear Turán conjecture.** If $G$ contains no linear path of length $k\ge 5$, then the number of edges in $G$ is at most

$$
\frac{k}{3}n+cn,
$$

for some universal constant $c$.

This conjecture asks for the linear Turán number of linear paths of length at least five, extending the known upper bound for linear 3-graphs without Berge paths. Its status is not established by the supplied text.

record.title: Clay's position-matrix eigenvalue conjectures for the single-shelf shuffle
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 3$, and let $M$ be the position matrix of a single-shelf shuffle, with

$$
M(i,j)=\frac{1}{2^i}\left(\binom{i-1}{j-1}+\binom{i-1}{n-j}\right),\quad 1\leq i,j\leq n.
$$

For a vector $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$, write $v(k)$ for its $k$th coordinate.

**Clay's position-matrix eigenvalue conjectures.** The following assertions hold:

1. $(1/4,v)$ is an eigenvalue-eigenvector pair of $M$, with multiplicity at least one, where

$$
v(k)=n^2-3nk+\frac{3}{2}k(k+1)-1.
$$

2. The non-zero eigenvalues of $M$ are $2^{-i}$, where $0\leq i\leq n-1$ is an even integer.

These conjectures concern the spectrum of the position matrix arising from the single-shelf shuffling model. The source attributes them to Clay and provides no evidence here that either conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: DP-completeness of exact circular chromatic index
record.statement:
Let $r\ge 3$ be a rational number. For a graph $G$, let $\chi_c'(G)$ denote its circular chromatic index, and let $\mathrm{CCHI}^{=_r}$ be the decision problem of determining whether $\chi_c'(G)=r$.

**DP-completeness conjecture.** The problem $\mathrm{CCHI}^{=_r}$ is DP-complete.

The preceding complexity discussion establishes NP-completeness for deciding whether $\chi_c'(G)\le r$ and explains why exact equality also involves a coNP component; the claimed DP-completeness is proposed on that basis.

record.title: The multicolored cycle matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cycle of length $2\ell$ whose edges are colored with $h$ colors. Let $M_0$ and $M_1$ be the perfect matchings consisting of the even and odd edges, respectively, and let $p_M\in\mathbb Z_+^h$ record the number of edges of each color in a matching $M$. Let $k\in\mathbb Z^h$ lie on the segment between $p_{M_0}$ and $p_{M_1}$. **The multicolored cycle matching conjecture.** There is a matching $M$ of size at least $\ell-h+2$ such that

$$
p_M\leq k
$$

component-wise and

$$
\lVert p_M-k\rVert_1\leq h-2.
$$

The paper presents this as a generalization of the corresponding three-color result and as a possible ingredient for extending the approximation guarantee to graphs with a constant number $h\geq4$ of colors. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.

record.title: Leonida–Li's weighted third-eigenvalue conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_n$ denote the set of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices with entries in $[0,1]$, and let $\lambda_1(M)\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n(M)$ be the eigenvalues of $M$. **Leonida–Li's weighted third-eigenvalue conjecture.** One has

$$
\inf_{M\in\mathcal{S}_n}\lambda_{n-1}(M)\geq -\frac{n}{3}.
$$

This weighted analogue was formulated to attack the open problem of whether every graph of order $n\geq 3$ satisfies $\lambda_3(G)\leq\lfloor n/3\rfloor$; the source does not indicate that the weighted conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: Superbrick conjecture for globally linked pairs in body-hinge graphs
record.statement: Let $H$ be a multigraph, let $G_H$ be the body-hinge graph induced by $H$, and let $d\geq 3$. A $k$-superbrick is the graph-theoretic object defined in the source for the multigraph under consideration, and $(\binom{d+1}{2}-1)H$ is obtained by replacing every edge of $H$ by $\binom{d+1}{2}-1$ parallel copies. **Body-hinge global linkedness conjecture.** A pair $\{u,v\}$ is globally $d$-linked in $G_H$ if and only if there is a $\binom{d+1}{2}$-superbrick $S$ of $(\binom{d+1}{2}-1)H$ containing the vertices of the bodies of $u$ and $v$. This conjecture extends the body-bar cluster characterization to body-hinge graphs; the source introduces it after proving the corresponding body-bar result, and no resolution is supplied in the given text.

record.title: Sharp rank-$2n-2$ equalizer bound for monomorphisms
record.statement:
Let $n\ge 3$, let $F_n$ be a free group of rank $n$, and let $F$ be a free group. Let $g,h:F_n\to F$ be monomorphisms. **Sharp equalizer rank conjecture.** Then

$$
\operatorname{rk}\operatorname{Eq}(g,h)\le 2n-2.
$$

The paper constructs examples attaining rank at least $2n-2$, motivating this as a candidate for the correct sharp upper bound after the Stallings equalizer conjecture was disproved. Its status is open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Jialin Lei and Teng Zhang, “Colored Stallings graphs and Counterexamples to Stallings equalizer conjecture”, arXiv:2604.24502 (2026).

record.title: Adiprasito–Kazhdan–Ziegler partition-rank versus analytic-rank conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a finite field, let $d\geq 2$ be an integer, and let

$$
f\in\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb{K}^{n_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb{K}^{n_d},\mathbb{K}).
$$

Here $\operatorname{PR}_{\mathbb{K}}(f)$ is the partition rank and $\operatorname{AR}_{\mathbb{K}}(f)$ is the analytic rank of $f$. **Adiprasito–Kazhdan–Ziegler's partition-rank versus analytic-rank conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{PR}_{\mathbb{K}}(f)\asymp_d\operatorname{AR}_{\mathbb{K}}(f).
$$

The relation $\asymp_d$ denotes linear equivalence with constants depending on $d$. The conjecture is known up to a logarithmic factor, but the exact linear equivalence remains open according to the source.

record.title: The EF1 conjecture for matroids with heterogeneous valuations
record.statement: Let $M=(E,\mathcal{I})$ be a matroid on the finite set of goods $E$, and let $\chi(M)$ be the least number of independent sets in a partition of $E$. Suppose $\chi(M)\leq n$ and there are $n$ agents with additive valuations $v_1,\ldots,v_n$. **The heterogeneous matroid EF1 conjecture.** There exists an EF1 partition of $E$ into $n$ independent sets of $M$. This is presented as a stronger version of the common-valuation matroid conjecture, and the source does not report a proof or disproof.

record.title: Häggkvist–Chetwynd line graph list-coloring conjecture
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, its **line graph** $L(G)$ has one vertex for each edge of $G$, with two vertices adjacent exactly when the corresponding edges share an endpoint. Let $\chi$ and $\chi_\ell$ denote the chromatic and list chromatic numbers. **Häggkvist–Chetwynd's conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\chi_\ell(L(G))=\chi(L(G)).
$$

This is the line-graph formulation of the List Edge Coloring Conjecture; the supplied text gives no general resolution.
record.source_name: Nandana K Vasudevan, K Somasundaram and N Narayanan, “List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability – A Dynamic Survey”, arXiv:2606.31702 (2026).

record.title: Bang-Jensen, Picasarri-Arrieta, and Yeo's characterization of champions
record.statement:
A tournament $H$ is a **champion** if there exists an integer $c_H$ such that every $H$-free tournament has acyclic dichromatic number at most $c_H$. The notation $TT_k$ denotes the transitive tournament on $k$ vertices, and $\Delta(1,1,k)\Rightarrow TT_k$ is interpreted using the tournament constructions defined in the source. **Bang-Jensen, Picasarri-Arrieta, and Yeo's conjecture.** A tournament $H$ is a champion if and only if $H$ is isomorphic to a subtournament of

$$
TT_k \Rightarrow (\Delta(1,1,k) \Rightarrow TT_k)
$$

for some integer $k\geq 1$. Since every champion is a hero but not every hero is a champion, this conjecture seeks a precise characterization of the tournaments whose exclusion gives a bounded acyclic dichromatic number.
record.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Pierre Charbit, Samuel Coulomb, Kathryn Nurse and Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta, “Acyclic Dichromatic Number of Tournaments: these are the Champions”, arXiv:2607.14694 (2026).
